input: Enroll in a defensive driving refresher course this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Defensive driving courses vary widely — some focus on safety habits, others on traffic law, and some are specifically designed to reduce points or satisfy insurance/court requirements. Knowing the purpose shapes which course type to target.
The course may be for the user alone or for multiple household members (e.g. a teen driver). This affects whether to seek individual enrollment or a group/family option.
Whether the user prefers in-person, online, or a hybrid format determines which providers and scheduling options are relevant, and how much flexibility they have.
Budget is a real filter — course costs range from free (some insurers) to $100+. Knowing a price ceiling narrows the search immediately.
The user's location (state/country) determines which accredited providers are legally valid, especially if the course must satisfy a court order, insurer, or DMV requirement.

Success could mean simply completing enrollment, finishing the course, or achieving a specific outcome like an insurance discount or point reduction. This defines what 'done well' actually looks like.
Some users want the shortest course possible; others want thorough instruction. Preferred course length and pace affect which options to prioritise.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a defensive driving refresher course this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and sign up for a defensive driving refresher course within the current month.

questions.title: Why do you need this course specifically?
questions.description: Is this to reduce license points, lower insurance premiums, satisfy a court or employer requirement, or purely for personal skill improvement? The purpose determines which course types are valid and worth considering.

questions.title: Is this course just for you or others too?
questions.description: Are you enrolling only yourself, or does another driver — such as a teen, partner, or employee — also need to complete the course? This affects whether to look for individual or multi-person enrollment options.

questions.title: Do you prefer online, in-person, or either format?
questions.description: Online courses offer flexibility, while in-person courses may be required for certain DMV or court purposes. Knowing your format preference immediately filters the provider list.

questions.title: What country and state or region are you in?
questions.description: Accredited providers vary by jurisdiction, and some courses are only valid for point reduction or insurance discounts in specific states or countries. Location is essential for finding a legally recognised option.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for this course?
questions.description: Course fees range from free (through some insurers) to over $100. A clear budget ceiling helps narrow options without wasting time on providers outside your range.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like for you?
questions.description: Is success simply getting enrolled this month, completing the course, receiving a certificate, or achieving a tangible result like an insurance discount or point removal? This defines the finish line.

questions.title: How long are you willing to spend on the course?
questions.description: Some courses are as short as 4 hours; others run over multiple days. Knowing your preferred time commitment helps prioritise courses that fit your schedule without feeling rushed or over-extended.
